global_rules: This chapter depicts early-to-mid twentieth-century Brazil: humid river and regional worlds can give way to Brazilian urban streets, civic courtyards, public halls, rail platforms, art-deco facades, mixed civilian dress, and local tropical vegetation where the narration moves beyond Belém.

Japanese woodblock editorial is the rendering language, never a geographic instruction. Do not generate Japanese tatami rooms, shoji, pagodas, kimonos, Japanese rooflines, Japanese crowd dress, or Japanese city views unless the narration explicitly calls for a Japanese visiting traveler.
Generated reconstruction is never historical evidence or a likeness. It may show anonymous social context but cannot identify a named person, assert a specific event, or contain factual text.

Do not generate readable writing, dates, flags, logos, citations, maps, route arrows, charts, relationship graphs, posters, blank books, cards, certificate-like surfaces, or fake archival documents. Local editorial layers own factual claims, citation, date, and map treatment.
Keep bodies, luggage, furniture, stages, platforms, and doors fully inside frame and visibly supported. History V4 prohibits multi-person grappling choreography and technical-instruction scenes.

Use crisp Combat Woodblock: sharp carved ink contours; broad flat deep indigo, ochre, rust, and jade fields; faint warm paper only; no photographic grit, heavy grain, muddy gradients, or faux archive damage.
